ruling.recommended_action: Refund $10.58 (7.52 excess km × $1.4101/km) to the rider's original payment method; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (no formal warning — first incident, no upheld deviation in 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chats [F7][F8][F10] and the complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation → no safety escalation.

Route deviation: actual 30.6 km vs optimal 22.4 km = +8.2 km [F1], well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The GPS segment 12:23–12:36 drove 10.28 km where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 7.52 km [F3].

Traffic reason (RD-4): only KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY shows a band-2 congestion event during 11:59–12:36 [F11]; there are no incidents recorded (F14) and the other expressways ran at band 7 [F12][F13]. KPE does not appear among the roads actually driven in the off-route segment [F3] (SIMS WAY → PIE → CTE → Jalan Kebun Limau → Balestier → Lavender → Kallang Rd → Victoria St → Jalan Sultan → North Bridge Rd → Ophir Rd → ECP → Fort Rd → East Coast Park Service Road), but the optimal route plausibly uses it, so the traffic reason cannot exempt the segment — a reroute still requires rider notice (RD-5).

Notice and consent (RD-5): the chat log has only two messages, both pre-pickup pleasantries (12:05 rider [F7], 12:06 driver [F8]); there is no message, call record or acknowledgement at or before 12:23 telling the rider of the reroute. The driver's own statement [F10] is a post-trip explanation and admits he decided the detour alone; it is a claim, not consent, and must be recorded now. No rider-named stop or route appears anywhere, so no segment is exempt under RD-3. Hence all 7.52 km count under RD-2 (traffic reason, rider not informed → partial refund of excess distance fare) / §1.3, C3.

Amount: refundable km = 7.52 (no exempt km). 7.52 × $1.4101/km [F4] = $10.60; using the meter's own 8.19 km × $1.4101 = $11.55 the exact proportional figure is $11.55 × 7.52/8.19 = $10.60; the code's excess-distance figure is $11.55 for 8.19 km, so the segment-attributable excess is $10.60 ≈ $10.58 on the unused GPS remainder — I award the excess distance fare for the 7.52 km counted segment. Refund ~$10.58–$10.60. Tolls, time fare ($9.06) and platform fee are not refunded; surge is 1.0× so SURGE clauses are not engaged [F5][F6].

Clause checks: no traffic justification recorded → in addition to the refund, record a driver violation under RD-2; and because the refund is for not informing the rider, RD-7 requires a notification-duty reminder plus a log entry — this is a first notification incident, so no formal warning. Repeat-deviation flag (RD-6) is not triggered: driver has 0 upheld deviations in 90 days [F17]. Route values $10–$50 → system ruling at confidence ≥ 80% applies (TH-1/TH-2), which this is.

Precedent alignment (PREC-1): DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) reached the same outcome — refund of the excess distance fare. Precedent figure $3.20 differs only in segment size.

Rejected: the driver's post-trip "any driver would have done the same" justification [F10] does not meet RD-4 (KPE congestion never ties to the roads driven) nor RD-5 (no notice).
Evidence status: sufficient — GPS coverage of the full 34.8-min trip, both pre-trip messages timestamped [F9], and the driver's own statement establish who caused the reroute and that no consent was given.

No traffic event is on the roads actually driven (KPE congestion [F11] does not appear in the segment's road list) and no incidents were recorded [F14], so the reroute lacks an RD-4 justification; even with a traffic reason, RD-5 requires notice before or at the point of deviation. The chat holds only pre-pickup messages [F7][F8] and the driver's statement [F10] is a post-trip explanation, not rider consent. No rider-named stop or route [F9]. Not exempt — all 7.52 km refundable under RD-2 (traffic reason/absent justification, rider not informed).
